subject: Sizing follow-up: crest vs basal throughput & streaming constraints
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@courierly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: Sizing follow-up: crest vs basal throughput & streaming constraints

Thanks again for the time today, Elena — good discussion. This thread is a short recap of what we heard on the call and the concrete asks so we can land on a recommended Dedicated sizing for your pilot.

Key signals from the call
- Primary product: conversational courier routing (streaming responses returned progressively).
- Two traffic modes: short interactive sessions (avg ~18 tokens/user-turn, many turns) and longer batch summarizations (avg ~3.6k tokens).
- Observed peaks: daily crest windows ~140–180 QPS for the interactive path (bursty, 30–120s buckets). Basal baseline outside peaks: ~12–18 QPS.
- Average tokens per second during crests (aggregate): ~56k tokens/sec across the fleet (derived from sample).

Clarifying numbers we need (please confirm or correct)
1) Peak concurrent streaming sessions during the crest window: you mentioned ~400 concurrent sessions — is that concurrent open websocket connections at peak?
2) Typical reply latency target for interactive path: P95 <= 180ms (end-to-end token emission) — are you flexible to P95 <= 250ms if batching is used?
3) For the long summarization jobs: are those latency-tolerant (minutes ok) and should they be scheduled on lower-cost reserved capacity?

Attached: courierly_workload_sample.csv (per-request token histograms) and a starter SLO matrix (proposed_slo_matrix.xlsx).

Next steps (I can action or loop infra as needed)
- Elena: confirm (1)-(3) above and add a short sample time window where the crest occurs (local timezone and hour).
- Redwood: we will convert the CSV into token/sec and QPS curves and send a sizing recommendation for Dedicated (baseline + 2 crest buffer strategies) by Thu EOD.
- Ops: Marissa/Stephanie to include suggested autoscale headroom and disk-backed KV cache notes once sizing is aligned.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Park <elena@courierly.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: Courierly SRE <sre@courierly.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 18:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Sizing follow-up: crest vs basal throughput & streaming constraints

Thanks Mateo — quick answers inline.

> 1) Peak concurrent streaming sessions during the crest window: you mentioned ~400 concurrent sessions — is that concurrent open websocket connections at peak?
Yes — we measured ~380–420 simultaneous open streaming connections during the 09:30–10:15 PST crest on weekdays. The crest is tied to our B2C morning batch push.

> 2) Typical reply latency target for interactive path: P95 <= 180ms — are you flexible to P95 <= 250ms if batching is used?
We can tolerate up to P95 <= 230ms in practice; anything above 250ms will materially degrade UX.

> 3) For the long summarization jobs: are those latency-tolerant (minutes ok) and should they be scheduled on lower-cost reserved capacity?
Correct — summarizations are background; 2–5 minute completion is fine and can be queued for reserved nodes.

Also attaching a short CSV export of the 09/14–09/20 crest windows; hope that helps.

Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product, Courierly

Attachment: courierly_crest_export_0914-0920.csv (CSV, 450KB)

Forwarding Elena's confirmations and the crest export. Highlights for ops:
- Confirmed peak concurrent streaming connections: 380–420 (use 420 for safety).
- P95 SLO: target 180ms desirable, 230ms acceptable.
- Long jobs are batchable and can run on reserved nodes with longer tails.

Diego / Marissa — can you run a quick estimate with these inputs? Suggested immediate model:
- Interactive path: reserve capacity sufficient for basal (18 QPS) + autoscale to handle crest up to 180 QPS sustained for 2m windows, with burst headroom to support 420 concurrent streams.
- Batch summarization: route to cheaper reserved pool, allow concurrency 8–16 jobs per node given 3.6k token avg.

Please add any caveats (KV cache warmup, prefix caching expectations, tokenization overhead) and put calculations in the shared sizing doc.

-Mateo

Quick sketch (I'll drop numbers into the doc and link):
- Basal footprint: size for 18 QPS interactive (~avg 12 tokens/turn => ~216 tokens/sec). Small cluster: 2 x gpus (low-concurrency) with autoscale floor.
- Crest handling: plan for sustained 180 QPS interactive during crest windows. With bursts to 420 concurrent streams, we recommend the following:
  * Primary pool: scale to handle 180 QPS sustained (estimate N mainstream GPUs).
  * Instant burst pool: smaller warm pool + fast-provision burst capacity to cover additional concurrency delta; prefer prewarmed containers with KV cache primed.
- Token cost / throughput: using Elena's CSV and our throughput curves, crest aggregate ~56k tokens/sec maps to ~X tokens/sec per GPU (I'll calculate X and place the exact GPU counts in the sheet).
- Batch summarization: route to reserved nodes with slower CPU-to-GPU handoff; allow long-tail completion up to 5 minutes.

Action items
- Marissa: populate the sizing workbook with exact GPU counts and per-GPU tokens/sec (today EOD).
- Diego: validate that prefix/KV cache warmup can be shared between streaming and non-streaming pools (identify cache TTL risks).
- Mateo: confirm with Elena whether crest windows repeat on weekends or only weekdays (we need to know scheduling).

I'll post the workbook link once numbers are in.

-Marissa
